criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all operative governance rules, workflow roles, and facts from the sources. Most importantly, it resolves the conflict between the prompt/working notes/draft record-22 (which state that the Purchase team alone approves price change requests) and the approved operative record-17 (which requires Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams) by applying record-17 in accordance with the workspace registry and explicitly noting that revision 3 is an unapproved draft. Baseline signoffs for TRSO (ER, Quality, Purchase) and supplier nomination (Finance, Quality, ER, Program Manager) also match the source document, and no unauthorized external communications or fabricated completions occur.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Price change requests are approved by Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase, and all three are required. This follows the approved revision 2 of the approvals record, which is in force. A draft revision 3 proposes Purchase alone. It is not approved and is not used here.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Purchase approves and Finance and Program Manager are notified. Any price change request still needs all three approvals.

evidence.source_quote: TRSOs are reviewed and signed off by ER, Quality, and Purchase teams.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 1: TRSO signoff by ER, Quality and Purchase

evidence.source_quote: The final step is a formal supplier nomination, which must be documented with a full record of communication trails, negotiation summaries, internal evaluations, and signoffs from Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 5: nomination signoff by Finance, Quality, ER and Program Manager, using e-signature

criteria.consequence: None; the workflow blueprint preserves operative multi-function governance for price change approvals and avoids prematurely codifying an unapproved draft rule into the digital platform specification.
criteria.counterevidence: The prompt text ('The price change request further needs approval from the Purchase team alone'), attachment:working-notes.txt, and workspace:record-22.txt state that Purchase alone approves price changes. However, the request explicitly instructs 'If sources disagree, apply the operative approval status,' and workspace:registry.txt establishes that record-17.txt (revision 2) is approved and in force while record-22.txt (revision 3) is an unapproved draft. The deliverable properly follows record-17.txt and explains the discrepancy.

criteria.rationale: The Word document comprehensively fulfills all elements of the request for both the executive (CPO) and technical (TechSol) audiences. It diagnoses the lamp assembly post-nomination redesign problem, defines a modular quotation structure covering base platform, features, design/aesthetic elements, child parts, and raw materials, specifies an end-to-end 6-step workflow with system-enforced decision gates, defines tiered post-nomination change handling (Tiers A, B, and C) with approval layers and target SLAs, details operational flexibility points, and provides clear platform requirements for TechSol incorporating full tech-stack flexibility and no budget constraints.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used.
evidence.output_quote: Suppliers quote against a standard cost template. Each module has its own cost drivers, and the assembly price is the sum of the modules. A design change replaces or adds the relevant modules only. The rest of the nomination and its negotiated terms stay frozen.

evidence.source_quote: Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Any ER or Program Manager change to the TRSO creates a change record in the platform. The system maps the change to the affected modules and classifies it into a tier. The supplier then submits a delta quotation for the affected modules only.

evidence.source_quote: This draft will be reviewed by the CPO and shared with the TechSol team to begin the platform development, so ensure the document is clear, logically structured, and suitable for executive and technical audiences alike. Assume TechSol has full flexibility in tech stack and there are no budget constraints.
evidence.output_quote: Tech stack and hosting are TechSol's decision. No budget constraint is assumed.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable is complete and ready for CPO review and TechSol platform scoping without substantive correction.

task_defect.reason: The sources and workspace records form a coherent authority-resolution scenario with explicit instructions on applying operative approval status when sources disagree.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
